tasks.title: Add single_writer_lock_is_exclusive — a single-writer lock so two `af run` processes can never share one TF_STATE_DIR
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn single_writer_lock_is_exclusive' tests/lock.rs && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
Goal: prevent two concurrent `af run` processes on the same TF_STATE_DIR from clobbering run-state.json (pi-durable's 'one process owns a storage at a time').

1. src/state.rs: add `impl Store { pub fn acquire_lock(&self) -> std::io::Result<LockGuard> }`.
   - Create `<state_dir>/.lock` (create the state dir first) atomically: write the file only if it does not exist (use OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true) — that is O_CREAT|O_EXCL). Put the current pid in it as text.
   - If it already exists: read the pid. If that process is ALIVE, return Err(io::Error::new(ErrorKind::Other, "another af owns this state dir (pid N)")). If the pid is DEAD (stale lock), reclaim it (overwrite with our pid) and succeed.
   - Determine liveness WITHOUT any new dependency; on unix shell out: Command::new("sh").args(["-c", &format!("kill -0 {pid}")]) and treat status.success() as alive.
   - Add `pub struct LockGuard` holding the state dir; its Drop removes `<state_dir>/.lock`.
2. src/run.rs: `run_loop` acquires the lock right after constructing `Store` (before the startup self-heal). On error print `config error: {err}` to stderr and return 2 — no worktree may be created. Hold the guard for the entire run, including `--once`.
3. tests/lock.rs: add `#[test] fn single_writer_lock_is_exclusive()` which:
   - builds a temp dir and two `Store` handles over it;
   - acquires on the first (must be Ok);
   - asserts the second `acquire_lock()` is `Err`;
   - drops the first guard, then asserts a third `acquire_lock()` is `Ok` (lock released on Drop);
   - writes a `.lock` file containing the pid of an already-reaped child process (spawn `sh -c 'exit 0'`, wait, use its pid) and asserts `acquire_lock()` succeeds (stale reclaim).
Keep the FULL existing test suite passing. The gate runs the whole suite plus `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

tasks.title: Add gate_replay_defaults_to_true_and_parses — a `gate_replay` task flag making acceptance-gate idempotency an explicit contract
tasks.accept: grep -q 'fn gate_replay_defaults_to_true_and_parses' tests/gate_replay.rs && cargo test && cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
tasks.acceptance_prose:
Goal: make gate replay-safety explicit (pi-durable marks read-only tools `replay: "safe"`; an effectful tool is never repeated).

1. src/config.rs: add `pub gate_replay: bool` to `Task`, annotated `#[serde(default = "default_true")]` (add a private `fn default_true() -> bool { true }`), so a tasks.json that omits the field parses as `true` and `"gate_replay": false` parses as false. Keep all existing derives and the struct's other fields compiling.
2. src/gate.rs: change `run_accept` to take the flag as a new final parameter `replay: bool`, and forward the decision to the gate process by appending the pair `("TF_GATE_REPLAY".to_string(), if replay { "1" } else { "0" }.to_string())` to the env slice passed to `subprocess::run`. Update gate.rs's three existing unit tests to pass `true`. Gate behavior is otherwise unchanged.
3. src/execute.rs: update the call site of `gate::run_accept` to pass `task.gate_replay`.
4. README.md: add a `gate_replay` row to the task-schema table, and state the contract: "the `accept` command MUST be idempotent; declare `gate_replay: false` for a gate with side effects — an interrupted such gate is settled as failed instead of re-run."
5. tests/gate_replay.rs: add `#[test] fn gate_replay_defaults_to_true_and_parses()` that writes TWO tasks.json files — one containing `"gate_replay": false`, one omitting the field — loads each with `config::load(...)` (reuse the minimal workers.json shape used in tests/cli.rs) and asserts `task.gate_replay == false` and `task.gate_replay == true` respectively.
Keep the full suite green; the gate also runs fmt + `clippy -D warnings`.
